short: Influence of processing route on microstructure and wear res
title: Influence of processing route on microstructure and wear resistance of fly ash reinforced AZ31 magnesium matrix composites

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: How the processing route (liquid stir casting vs solid-state FSP) changes FA dispersion, microstructure and wear of AZ31/FA composites is not established. Reinforce AZ31B magnesium alloy with 10 vol.% fly ash particles (~10 um, SiO2-rich).
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/gap), n2 (DES/modification), n3 (DES/variable_sweep), n4 (PRC/forming), n5 (PRC/forming)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: FSP composite has a homogeneous FA dispersion with no particle-free zones across the stir zone. Stir cast composite has an inhomogeneous FA dispersion: particle clusters beside particle-free regions at top, middle and bottom.

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Frictional heat plus intense strain drive dynamic recrystallization during FSP, with broken FA particles pinning boundaries, refining grains. FSP composite has higher hardness than the stir cast composite.
states.detail: Absorbed: m1 (MEC/pathway), p1 (PRP/value), p2 (PRP/value), m2 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Dynamic recrystallization during FSP is well acknowledged in literature [21]; Hall-Petch: finer grains raise hardness/strength; Protruding load-bearing hard particles reduce the pin-counterface contact area and hence friction

states.title: Performance state
states.head: FSP composite wears less in sliding: wear rate 280 vs 420 x1e-5 mm3/m (33% lower) and smaller final height loss
states.detail: Absorbed: f1 (PRF/service_capability). Premises: Archard's wear law: wear rate inversely proportional to hardness

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: FSP beats stir casting for AZ31/10 vol.% FA: homogeneous dispersion, ~4 um grains, reaction-free interfaces and 33% lower wear rate

nodes.title: MICRO, F3, F5
nodes.head: Dark particle clusters sit in some fields while neighbouring areas are particle-free, in all four fields (a-d). Dark particles are evenly scattered over all four fields with no particle-free areas
nodes.solves: Stir cast composite has an inhomogeneous FA dispersion: particle clusters beside particle-free regions at top, middle and bottom
nodes.note: Etched cellular network ~20-50 um visible; clusters often touch the network
nodes.necessity_reason: s4, s1 keeps shown support from o3 after removal.

nodes.title: DIFF, F2
nodes.head: SiO2 reflections at ~26.5 and ~58 deg are clearly taller in pattern b than in pattern a
nodes.solves: FSP composite has a homogeneous FA dispersion with no particle-free zones across the stir zone
nodes.note: Peak height is a weak proxy for dispersion; sampling depth and particle fragmentation also change it
nodes.necessity_reason: s1 keeps shown support from o7 after removal.

nodes.title: EBSD:IPF, F7
nodes.head: IPF map b shows equiaxed grains ~2-5 um; map a shows colour domains spanning ~150-400 um
nodes.solves: FSP refines the matrix to fine equiaxed grains (~4 um) versus coarse grains (~145 um) in the stir cast composite
nodes.note: Map a is largely unindexed speckle, far more than the ~10 um FA particles could account for; its domains look larger than the 145 um mean; caption says grain-boundary maps but no boundary lines are drawn
nodes.detail: o10: IPF map b shows equiaxed grains ~2-5 um; map a shows colour domains spanning ~150-400 um
nodes.necessity_reason: No member reaches image_support shown and s2 has no other figure-backed support.

nodes.title: MICRO, F1, F6
nodes.head: As-received FA: mixed spherical cenospheres and irregular angular particles, sizes ~1 to >25 um. Embedded particles are mostly ~2-15 um, several angular with sharp corners, amid fine debris; no large cenospheres as in F1
nodes.note: Caption says 2000x and 5000x but in-image Mag reads 1.00 KX and 2.00 KX Size reduction vs F1 is visible but modest; nanometric debris is not resolved at 2000x
nodes.necessity_reason: m1 keeps shown support from o11 after removal.

nodes.title: MICRO, F10
nodes.head: Worn surface b: shallower grooves covered by numerous fine debris particles, no large crater
nodes.solves: Uniformly dispersed FA stops asperities penetrating the subsurface; load-bearing FA layers fracture into fine debris that roll (three-body), reducing cutting
nodes.necessity_reason: m2 keeps shown support from o16, o17 after removal.

nodes.title: MECH:wear, PROCESS, F9
nodes.head: Height loss vs time: stir casting reaches ~350 um and FSP ~240 um at ~1160 s; stir cast curve is jagged with sudden drops. FSP height loss exceeds stir casting for the first ~300 s; the curves cross between ~300 and ~400 s
nodes.solves: FSP composite wears less in sliding: wear rate 280 vs 420 x1e-5 mm3/m (33% lower) and smaller final height loss
nodes.op: compare across conditions, read characteristic point, read trend
nodes.note: 240/350 gives ~31% less height loss, close to the stated 33% wear-rate gain; FSP curve is perfectly smooth, possibly smoothed Text reports only the end-of-test wear rate; running-in favours stir casting. The jagged stir-cast curve first reaches the FSP curve near 300 s and dips below it again at ~410 s before staying above
